newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish bonds up in line with international markets.
newsitem.headline: Irish bonds up in line with international markets.

text.p: Irish government bonds were up along the curve in thin late trade on Friday in line with international markets after the release of U.S. data, dealers said.
Dealers said U.S. Treasuries had firmed after a surprisingly weak January PPI number, showing a drop of 0.3 percent, and unchanged January factory output figures.
"There was not really that much action at all. We did see interest in the 10-year area but overall we have performed in line with other international markets," one dealer said.
"U.S. Treasuries got a good boost from the PPI data around lunchtime today. That provided a spur to international markets," one dealer said.

By 1640 GMT, the 6.5 percent bond due 2001 was up 15 pence from Thursday's close at 103.55 to yield 5.60 percent while the benchmark eight percent bond due 2006 was up 50 pence at 111.70 to yield 6.31 percent.
Irish bonds were trading at 152 basis points over German bunds in the five-year area and 85 basis points over Germany in the 10-year area, dealers said.
Dealers said the market awaited Tuesday's domestic auctions which they expect will go well.
"Monday is a day off in the U.S. (Washington's birthday) so Tuesday's domestic auctions are the focus. We expect they will go quite well," the dealer said.
Ireland's National Treasury Management Agency (NTMA) plans to auction 150 million punts of the 6.5 percent bond due 2001 in a competitive auction for primary dealers on February 18.
Up to 30 million punts of the stock will also be offered in a non-competitive auction, the NTMA said.
